reference.title: Lever Leg Extension
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page was not opened from the authoring environment, so the data sheet was not read and the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as the legs straighten, breathe in as they come back down.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s up, short squeeze, about 2.3 s down

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Stack load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can lift to straight legs without the hips lifting off the seat.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then one plate; slower lowering

cues.text: Sit with your back on the pad and the knee joints in line with the machine pivot; the roller rests on the front of the shins just above the ankles; hold the side handles.
Breathe out and straighten both knees, lifting the roller in an arc until the legs are long.
Squeeze the front of the thighs at the top for a moment; keep the hips down on the seat.
Breathe in and lower slowly under control until the knees are back at about 90 degrees.
Pause briefly at the bottom without letting the stack touch down.

mistakes.mistake: Knees out of line with the pivot
mistakes.fix: Set the back pad so the knee joint lines up with the machine axis; the roller then stays put on the shin.
Lift smoothly; pause at the top instead of swinging.
Pull down on the side handles and lighten the stack.

mistakes.mistake: Dropping the weight on the way down
mistakes.fix: Take about two seconds to lower.

kinematics.norm: From about 90 degrees to nearly straight (clinical opinion)
Knee joint in line with the machine pivot so the roller does not slide on the shin (clinical opinion)
On the front of the lower shin, just above the ankle (clinical opinion)
Seated, back on the pad; hips do not move (clinical opinion)
Open-chain knee extension loads the knee most near full extension, unlike the squat (Escamilla et al. 1998)
Controlled, about 1-1.5 s up and 2-3 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Lever Leg Extension, video (movement reference)
Escamilla et al. 1998, biomechanics of the knee during closed kinetic chain and open kinetic chain exercises (Med Sci Sports Exerc 30(4):556-569; PubMed 9565938)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
The stack load is user-chosen: start light and lift without jerking.
Knee pain at the front of the knee: shorten the range (stop short of full extension) or skip the exercise and ask a clinician.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Front-of-knee discomfort: work in a shorter range, for example from 90 to 45 degrees.
Uneven legs: one leg at a time with half the load.
regressions: Seated knee extension with no load.
progressions: Slower lowering with a 2 s pause at the top.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Prime mover: straightens the knee; open-chain extension works the quadriceps hardest near straight legs (Escamilla et al. 1998).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Prime mover: straightens the knee; open-chain extension works the quadriceps hardest near straight legs (Escamilla et al. 1998).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Lengthen at the top with the knee straight; they do not lift the load.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Lengthen at the top with the knee straight; they do not lift the load.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the pelvis still on the seat.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Hold the side handles to keep the hips down.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Hold the side handles to keep the hips down.
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Keep the thighs on the seat.
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Keep the thighs on the seat.
